To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RAD6 is a central component of an E2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, which targets N end rule substrated to the lysosome for degradation.

we have identified KCMF1 as a novel binding partner of RAD6, a protein with roles in DNA damage repair and transcription, that KCMF1 interacts with RAD6 at the lysosome, and that disruption to the RAD6 KCMFM1 interaction may contribute to XLID in some patients.

RAD6 is a key component of a novel E2 E3 ubiquitination complex that is required for lysosome mediated protein degradation, and which may be disrupted in X linked intellectual dis ability (XLID) via point mutations in the RAD6A gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of new E2 and E3 ubiquitin ligases that are involved in the regulation of protein homeostasis.
understanding the role of the ubiquitin E2 RAD6 in a number of biological processes including transcriptional regulation, cell cycle regulation and DNA repair.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate cell proliferation and cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KCM1-Rad6-UBR4 interaction is a novel and important regulatory mechanism for ubiquitin mediated protein degradation.

RAD6A mutations in XLID patients could affect the interaction of the protein with KCMF 1 and UBR 4, which could in turn alter the activity of the E2 E3 ubiquitin complex, and thus affect the lysosome mediated degradation of unknown N end rule containing substrates.
KCMF1 interacts with RAD6A and UBR4 and that this complex may be involved in the regulation of late endosome/lysosome trafficking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

RAD6 is a multi-functional E2 that interacts with a large number of different proteins and complexes, and that it can act in a number of biological processes including DNA damage repair, transcription, and now, lysosome mediated degradation.
KCMF1, a protein that has been previously implicated in the regulation of potassium channels, is also involved in the regulation of late endosome vesicles.
